title: What If You Drilled Into a Lake Hidden Under Antarctica?

scenes.text: What if you drilled into a lake buried under Antarctica? Russians did. The water shot up the hole.
Lake Vostok sits under about 3,770 meters of ice, more than two miles, in the coldest place on Earth.
Vostok Station once recorded minus 129 degrees Fahrenheit above it. Below it, the water stays liquid.
The lake covers roughly 14,000 square kilometers. That is larger than many countries' biggest lakes.
Some scientists think it has been sealed off for 15 to 20 million years or more.
In February 2012 the drill broke through, and water under pressure from the ice rose up the borehole.

description:
